screens.title: Approved work, by state
screens.description: A board of approved work, with a selectable list in each lifecycle column.
screens.note: Click any card to select it; Enter opens the item. Left/right changes state column; up/down changes item. Drafts are a separate collection.

screens.title: All approved work in a selectable table
screens.description: A row table of approved work; Drafts are excluded.
screens.note: Every issue row is selectable. Drafts never appear in this approved-work table.

screens.title: Draft ideas stay in their own inbox
screens.description: A separate draft inbox, all types, no approved work.
screens.note: Every issue row is selectable. Drafts never appear in this approved-work table.

screens.title: Improve process status colors
screens.description: Visible submenu depth, context and next gate.
screens.note: The breadcrumb, nested issue navigation, raised panel and back action make submenu depth visible. Escape restores the parent selection.

screens.title: Accounts, capacity and permissions in one workspace
screens.description: Dedicated Accounts workspace with provider identity, usage bars and defaults.
screens.note: Accounts is a top-level destination. Usage bars label percent used and reset time; no aggregate across incomparable provider limits.

screens.title: Supervise sessions with capacity in context
screens.description: Selectable sessions and account capacity in context.
screens.note: Task rows, status badges, provider accents and account usage have distinct roles. Selecting never takes terminal control.

screens.title: Terminal input has a visible boundary
screens.description: Observe and Control have distinct input and navigation boundaries.
screens.note: Control is styled amber and fills the workspace body. Ctrl+] is the only application escape in terminal input mode.

screens.title: Settings has visible sections and explicit scope
screens.description: Visible settings category, nested section, scope and local preference preview.
screens.note: The top-level Settings workspace replaces hidden preference overlays. Category, nested section, scope and back path remain visible.

screens.title: A full redesign for the worktree workspace
screens.description: Worktrees is redesigned within the shared five-tab application shell.
screens.note: Worktrees gets the same five-tab shell, shaded selection, breadcrumb and contextual controls. Existing shortcuts remain scoped to this workspace.
